history.summary: An over-200-year-old Hanuman temple on the east bank of the Lower Lake (Bada Talab) in Jahangirabad, Bhopal. It was built by Sri Rai Chalanlal, a devotee of Hanuman who was a royal courtier, on land donated by Nawab Jahangir Muhammad Khan; the pranapratishta of the deity was performed in 1840. The main idol is in ardha shila roop (half-sculpted form), facing east with the temple door facing north, holding a gadha (mace) in the left hand and the right hand in abhaya mudra. Local lore says the idol was found in the waters of the Lower Lake, while other accounts say saints from Ayodhya installed it — flagged as unverified variants. A National Green Tribunal inspection report (OA 208/2024) gives the temple's coordinates as 23°15'1.1736"N, 77°24'37.3428"E and records four shrines in the premises. Note: sources variously say 'Lower Lake' and 'Chhota Talab' — the two lakes adjoin at this point, so the discrepancy is minor.

name: Khatlapura Mandir
town_description: Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh, is known as the City of Lakes for its two artificial lakes (Upper and Lower) built centuries ago. It is one of India's greenest cities, blending Nawabi heritage — mosques, palaces and bazaars — with modern institutions and museums.
